name: Bio-Oil

lead: Bio-Oil is a branded skincare oil used on scars, stretch marks and uneven tone, with the aim of making these areas look softer and smoother.

Its moisturizing oils soften the skin surface. Product-specific trials were not found, and a Cochrane review summarized on Wikipedia found no evidence that creams or oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy.

paras: People massage it into the area once or twice daily as part of a routine, usually for months, and it is often paired with sun protection on scars.
It is a cosmetic, not a drug, so it is not subject to drug approval. No safety data were found in the sources reviewed, and individual skin reactions to any topical product are possible.

chain: Scars and stretch marks look softer
angle.text: Users massage this cosmetic oil into scars, stretch marks and uneven tone so the skin looks softer and more supple. It works as a moisturizer, and product-specific trials were not found.

lead: Bio-Oil is a branded skincare oil that people apply to the skin with the aim of making scars, stretch marks and uneven skin tone look smoother and more even. It is sold as a cosmetic over the counter, and its use is a daily moisturising routine: the oil is massaged into the area of concern, which keeps skin soft and supple while the user waits for marks to mature and fade.

Stretch marks (striae) and scars are common appearance concerns. Stretch marks appear in areas of stored fat such as the abdomen, thighs, hips and breasts, most often in young women and during pregnancy, puberty, weight gain or muscle gain.[1] That makes them a topic for people who bulk, gain muscle quickly or lose weight, and a body-oil routine is one of the most widely used responses.

Peer-reviewed trials of the Bio-Oil product itself are not summarised in the general references consulted for this article. For the wider category, Wikipedia reports that a systematic review (a Cochrane review by Brennan and colleagues, 2012) did not find evidence that creams and oils prevent or reduce stretch marks in pregnancy, and describes tretinoin, hyaluronic acid and lasers as other approaches that have been tried.[1]
infobox: Scars, stretch marks, uneven skin tone

paras: The product is positioned for three appearance goals: fading the look of scars, softening the look of stretch marks, and improving uneven skin tone. Wikipedia notes that stretch marks are most often seen on the abdomen, breasts, thighs, hips and buttocks and affect young women the most; about 90 percent of pregnant women are affected, with higher risk in teenagers and with large weight gain.[1]
Other triggers listed include rapid growth, weight gain, muscle gain and corticosteroid use, which is why people who build muscle or change weight quickly sometimes reach for a body oil.[1]

sections.h: Context: what is known about stretch mark treatments
paras: Wikipedia reports that no clearly effective treatment exists once stretch marks have formed. Topical tretinoin 0.1 percent has been effective on early stretch marks in several studies, hyaluronic acid is said to improve their appearance, and lasers, glycolic acid and microdermabrasion have been tried.[1]

The same article cites the Cochrane review finding that evidence for creams and oils preventing or reducing stretch marks in pregnancy was not found.[1] The Bio-Oil product is not named in that summary.

No studies found for the branded product in the general references consulted. A search of the biomedical literature for the term "bio-oil" mainly returns work on biofuel produced from biomass, which is unrelated to the skincare product. Studies of other oils and creams for stretch marks are summarised in the Cochrane review described above.[1]

The oil is mentioned in skincare discussions as a popular over-the-counter option for scars and stretch marks, often alongside moisturisers and retinoids. No forum material specific to the product was available for this article.
